title: Reduce elbow pain with 0 effort in less than a minute
summary: Lifters grip constantly (bench, squat, deadlift) but never train the opposite motion, opening the hand, and this imbalance can cause elbow pain. His fix is doing hand-opening reps against small IronMind elastics through the day, between sets and after gripper work. He explains band placement on the fingers to get the right difficulty.

claims.claim: Lifters grip constantly, since bench, squat and deadlift all involve gripping the bar, but almost never train the opposite motion: opening the hand.
Training should include opposite movements and antagonist muscles; hand opening is neglected because there are no machines for it and plain reps seem pointless.
Opening and closing the hand differ like opening and closing the jaw: similar muscles, different action; training only one causes imbalances, as with people who clench their jaw all day.
Elbow pain may come from all your grip work rather than from pushing or extension exercises.
IronMind hand-extensor elastics are cheap (about 9 dollars a bag) and his have lasted 3 years without breaking, but any elastic works.
Wrap an elastic around your fingers and open the hand as often as possible; it relaxes the constantly tensed forearm muscles and has a big effect on elbow health.
Hand-opening band work isn't taxing, so do it during the day at school or the computer, between sets, and especially after gripper work.
Even lifters with strong grips and big forearms must start with the thinnest elastics because the hand-opening muscles are weak from never being trained.
The closer the elastic is to the fingertips the harder it is; near the knuckles it does nothing; too high hurts the knuckle, so place it just below the first knuckle.
If one finger is fragile (his thumb), lower the band on that finger to give it better leverage while keeping the stimulus.

exercises.name: Elastic band finger extensions (hand opening)
cues: band just below the first knuckle
lower it on a fragile finger
exercises.why: trains the antagonist of gripping, relieves forearm tension and elbow pain
